liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Unhurried, attentive Dark Star that follows the contours of the classic Live/Dead version; Reviewer describes Dark Star with a roughly 20-minute opening guitar solo by Jerry [4][11][14]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Schoolgirl excellent, part of a raunchy Pigpen stretch interrupted by a below-average Doin' That Rag; Big harmonica part in Schoolgirl, with the harp competing with Jerry's guitar for solo space [3][11]
- **Turn On Your Love Light** (1 review): Both Dark Star and Lovelight run over twenty minutes, per the reviewer [12]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Jerry's wailing, southern-rock-flavored runs fill this Dew, more a flurry of licks than a slow-building climax [6]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): Reviewer especially loves the St. Stephen into The Eleven transition, preferring this era's jams to the 1970s [10]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Eleven huge and a must-hear, wondering why reviews overlook it [8]
- **Death Don't Have No Mercy** (1 review): Reviewer finds Death Don't Have No Mercy beautiful and poetic [14]
- **Drums** (1 review): Reviewer hears no Caution; thinks it was Drums into a Jam, typical of the period, then cut [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-04-13.sbd.miller.87378.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 11 songs; 119 min; rated 3.91/5 by 23 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is good but not perfect: slight hiss and a few defects [11]
- **gd69-04-13.sbd.cotsman.6287.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 120 min; rated 3.64/5 by 14 [2]. Said about its sound: The end of Lovelight is cut off in this soundboard, which loses Pigpen working the crowd; Several minutes are lost to cuts at end of Lovelight and start of Doin' That Rag; A minor splice occurs about ten minutes into Dark Star [2][3]

## Around the show

- The show's ending is missing, likely a Caution, as suggested by the jam out of Drums [2]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-04-13.sbd.miller.87378.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD [1]
- **gd69-04-13.sbd.cotsman.6287.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dan Zymanski and J. Cotsman; source: Soundboard [2]
